prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: השוואת דירות להשכרה בתל אביב (language he, right-to-left: column 1 is on the RIGHT).
Grid: 5 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 13px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "שכונה" · longest unbreakable word 58px · one-line width 76px
  col 2: header "מחיר" · longest unbreakable word 37px · one-line width 90px
  col 3: header "חדרים" · longest unbreakable word 37px · one-line width 37px
  col 4: header "קומה" · longest unbreakable word 37px · one-line width 122px
  col 5: header "הערות" · longest unbreakable word 70px · one-line width 941px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 584px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 583px.
Fixed: content, font, 13px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 584px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"Compare rental apartments in Tel Aviv by neighborhood, monthly price, size, floor and descriptive notes.","reading":"Readers scan the neighborhood names to identify listings, compare the numeric attributes across rows, then read the notes for details and tradeoffs.","groups":["Neighborhood identifies each listing; price and rooms are the primary comparison fields.","Floor and elevator availability describe accessibility; the floor cell combines both.","Notes contain longer qualitative details and benefit most from flexible width."],"keep_intact":["Neighborhood names where possible, especially multiword names.","Prices and their currency symbols; room counts and decimal values.","Floor numbers and short floor expressions."],"may_wrap":["Long notes can wrap naturally between words.","Elevator descriptions can wrap after the floor information.","The monthly price qualifier can wrap if necessary; note wrapping may already set the row height."]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[97,111,58,143,174],"idea":"Keep neighborhood, price and floor entries on one line and concentrate wrapping in the notes."},{"name":"B","widths":[97,111,58,100,217],"idea":"Preserve the main comparison fields while allowing floor descriptions to wrap, giving the notes more space."},{"name":"C","widths":[85,85,58,85,270],"idea":"Prioritize readable notes by compacting neighborhood, price and floor columns and using the resulting row height for their wrapping."}]}
